# Configuration reference

Every setting the control plane reads, with its default. All of them are environment variables
prefixed `FLEETWARD_`; the names below are written without the prefix, so `HTTP_ADDR` is set as
`FLEETWARD_HTTP_ADDR`.

Two parsing rules are worth knowing before reading the table. **An empty value counts as unset**, so
exporting a variable to the empty string restores its default rather than clearing it. And a
*malformed* number, duration, or boolean falls back to its default rather than failing to start —
which means a typo in a duration is silent, and the value you get is the one in this table.

## Environment

| Variable | Default       |           | Notes |
| -------- | ------------- | --------- | --- |
| `ENV`    | `development` | validated |  |

## Logging

| Variable         | Default |           | Notes |
| ---------------- | ------- | --------- | --- |
| `LOG_ADD_SOURCE` | `false` |           | AddSource includes file and line in every record. Useful in development, noisy in production. |
| `LOG_FORMAT`     | `text`  | validated | Format is "json" for production pipelines or "text" for a readable development console. |
| `LOG_LEVEL`      | `info`  | validated | Level is one of debug, info, warn, error. |

## Metadata store

The only truly critical dependency: the control plane will not start without it.

| Variable                   | Default                                                                   |              | Notes |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | --- |
| `METADB_AUTO_MIGRATE`      | `true`                                                                    |              | AutoMigrate runs pending migrations at startup. Convenient in development; in production most operators prefer to run migrations as a deliberate, separate step. |
| `METADB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`   | `10s`                                                                     |              |  |
| `METADB_DSN`               | `postgres://fleetward:fleetward@localhost:5432/fleetward?sslmode=disable` | **required** | DSN is a libpq-style connection string. It contains a password and must never be logged. |
| `METADB_MAX_CONN_LIFETIME` | `1h`                                                                      |              |  |

## Secrets

The security of every stored credential reduces to the protection of the master key.

| Variable                  | Default   |              | Notes |
| ------------------------- | --------- | ------------ | --- |
| `SECRETS_MASTER_KEY`      | *(empty)* |              | MasterKey is a base64-encoded 32-byte key for the aesgcm provider. Prefer MasterKeyFile: an environment variable is visible to anything that can read /proc. |
| `SECRETS_MASTER_KEY_FILE` | *(empty)* | **required** | MasterKeyFile points at a mounted file containing the base64-encoded key. |
| `SECRETS_PROVIDER`        | `aesgcm`  |              | Provider is "aesgcm" for the MVP provider or "vault" once that lands. |

## Verification sandboxes

The `kubernetes` provider is not implemented; `docker` is the only working value.

| Variable                  | Default     |  | Notes |
| ------------------------- | ----------- | --- | --- |
| `SANDBOX_DOCKER_HOST`     | *(empty)*   |  |  |
| `SANDBOX_LABEL_PREFIX`    | `fleetward` |  | LabelPrefix marks containers Fleetward owns, so an orphan sweep can find them after a crash. |
| `SANDBOX_MAX_LIFETIME`    | `2h`        |  | MaxLifetime is a hard ceiling after which a sandbox is destroyed regardless of state. It is the backstop behind the normal deferred cleanup, not a replacement for it. |
| `SANDBOX_NETWORK`         | *(empty)*   |  | Network attaches sandboxes to a specific Docker network. Empty uses the default bridge. |
| `SANDBOX_PROVIDER`        | `docker`    |  | Provider is "docker" in the MVP; "kubernetes" is the planned second implementation. |
| `SANDBOX_STARTUP_TIMEOUT` | `3m`        |  | StartupTimeout bounds how long a sandbox may take to become ready before verification is reported inconclusive. |

## Engine plugins

| Variable                      | Default         |  | Notes |
| ----------------------------- | --------------- | --- | --- |
| `PLUGINS_DIR`                 | `./bin/plugins` |  | Dir holds the plugin binaries, named fleetward-plugin-<engine>. |
| `PLUGINS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`   | `30s`           |  | HandshakeTimeout bounds how long a plugin may take to become usable after launch. |
| `PLUGINS_HEALTH_INTERVAL`     | `30s`           |  | HealthInterval is how often the manager probes a running plugin. |
| `PLUGINS_MAX_RESTARTS`        | `0`             |  | MaxRestarts caps consecutive restart attempts before the plugin is marked failed. Zero means keep retrying at the maximum backoff forever. |
| `PLUGINS_RESTART_BACKOFF_MAX` | `5m`            |  |  |
| `PLUGINS_RESTART_BACKOFF_MIN` | `1s`            |  | RestartBackoffMin and RestartBackoffMax bound the exponential backoff between restarts of a crashing plugin. |

## Scheduler

Parsed and cross-validated, and read by nothing — there is no scheduler yet.

| Variable                        | Default |  | Notes |
| ------------------------------- | ------- | --- | --- |
| `SCHEDULER_ENABLED`             | `true`  |  |  |
| `SCHEDULER_LEASE_HEARTBEAT`     | `30s`   |  | LeaseHeartbeat is how often a running job renews its lease. |
| `SCHEDULER_LEASE_TTL`           | `2m`    |  | LeaseTTL is how long a claimed job stays claimed without a heartbeat. It must comfortably exceed the heartbeat interval, never the job duration: long jobs renew rather than hold. |
| `SCHEDULER_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS` | `4`     |  | MaxConcurrentJobs caps jobs running on this control-plane instance. |
| `SCHEDULER_POLL_INTERVAL`       | `10s`   |  | PollInterval is how often a runner looks for claimable work. |

## Required

`METADB_DSN` must be non-empty, and a master key must be supplied when the secrets provider is
`aesgcm` — either `SECRETS_MASTER_KEY` or `SECRETS_MASTER_KEY_FILE`. Enabling TLS on a listener
requires its certificate and key. Enabling authentication requires an issuer URL.

With `ENV=production`, authentication may not be disabled and issuer verification may not be
skipped. Note what production mode does **not** require: TLS on any listener, TLS to the metadata
store or the object store, or a master key held in a file rather than an environment variable. A
production configuration therefore passes validation while serving plain HTTP — and while demanding
an authentication layer that does not exist yet.
